thread:
anya: putting this here in case others hit it  Next.js middleware crashes at import time with 'Reference to node:crypto' after we upgraded the SDK. Edge runtime rejects it immediately. anyone found a tidy pattern that avoids a separate package?

samir: we use a single package with an explicit edge subpath export, eg import from 'pkg/edge'. build a tiny edge ESM bundle that excludes node builtins. no need for two npm packages.

miko: exact steps that worked for us:
1) add src/edge-entry.ts that only imports edge-safe modules
2) esbuild: platform=browser, format=esm, target=es2020, external: ['node:crypto','fs']
3) package.json exports: {"./edge": {"import": "./dist/edge.mjs"}}
4) ship dist/edge.d.ts and add typesVersions mapping for the './edge' subpath
then middleware: import { create } from 'pkg/edge'

anya: does typesVersions reliably make VSCode pick up the types for the subpath? sometimes TS resolution is gnarly in monorepos.

samir: yes, typesVersions is the most compatible route across tsc/VSCode versions. example: "typesVersions": {"*": {"./edge": ["dist/edge.d.ts"]}}. also include a dist/edge.d.ts file so editors that don't look at typesVersions still get a file.

miko: watch transitive deps. our metrics client pulled in node:fs indirectly. we replaced it with an edge-safe noop shim for the edge build (alias in rollup/esbuild).

anya: CI caught ours too only when deploying to staging, odd that dev didn't fail. any tips to reproduce locally?

samir: bundle your edge artifact with esbuild and run it under Miniflare (Cloudflare Workers' dev) or Node's --experimental-wasm-modules isn't equivalent. also run `node -e "console.log(require.resolve('pkg/edge'))"` from the app workspace to ensure resolution matches what you expect.

miko: we added a tiny runtime guard to dist/edge.mjs that throws early if a Node global is present so CI fails fast with a clear message instead of a mysterious import error in prod.

anya: great pointers, we'll try the subpath + edge build + typesVersions + runtime guard. thanks! :raised_hands:
